system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “STANDARD”, “FINAL”, “agreed” and “pre-cleared” labels are not buyer authority. **No Amelia Frost approval has been given** for the cap or claims-period fallbacks. The underlying DD records have not been supplied here; the Disclosure Letter’s summaries require verification and refreshing.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | 20% / AUD 4.8m. | 25% / AUD 6m; 20% only with Amelia’s prior written authority identifying the draft. | **Counter at 25%.** Matching a conditional fallback does not authorise its acceptance. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, recovering only the excess. | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket, recovering qualifying claims from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Replace both thresholds and basket mechanics.** The draft materially excludes otherwise recoverable losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notice within 18 months; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | 24 months for general warranties; 18 months only with Amelia’s written approval; separately specified category regimes. | **Counter at 24 months and delete the blanket extension.** Neither the fallback nor cross-category application is authorised. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general caps and deadlines. | Separate 100% / AUD 24m cap, at least six years, outside general basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar. | **Reject general-regime treatment.** Ownership and capacity risks require distinct protection. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims without an express exception. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert an overriding, non-waivable carve-out.** The blanket drafting would restrict protections that nobody may waive under the playbook. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Whole-data-room, Accounts, statutory-register and public-record general disclosure. | Specific fair disclosure sufficiently explaining the nature and scope of each relevant matter; no deemed disclosure through data-room access, registers or prudent searches. | **Reject blanket disclosure and require specific disclosures.** Mere availability of information must not defeat warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for buyer/adviser knowledge, including discoverable data-room or public-record matters. | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any seller-knowledge qualification must identify named seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Delete clause 8.3 as proposed.** It shifts undiscovered and inadequately disclosed risks onto the buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent, although no final consent or satisfaction evidence is supplied. | Effective consent **and evidence all associated conditions are satisfied before Completion**. | **Retain a substantive Completion condition and obtain current evidence.** Delivery alone does not establish effective consent for a customer representing approximately 30% of revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; security release after Completion; no repayment or final discharge supplied. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; deferred release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia’s approval. | **Require a documented Completion discharge mechanism.** The proposed unsecured promise leaves debt/security exposure after closing. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional bonuses treated as a seller matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Explicit funds-flow line item or demonstrable seller funding for payable bonuses plus triggered on-costs, with employment conditions and payroll treatment verified. | **Correct the funds flow and confirm funding and on-costs.** Calling bonuses a seller matter does not fund the Completion-triggered liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 shown open internally; no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Broader protection for Ironquay ownership, assignment and infringement exposure, preserving the SOW3 payment/transfer cure; independently verify payment and transfer status. | **Broaden the indemnity and pursue the cure.** The narrow payment indemnity may not address IP defects, and AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary, said not to be material; possible export of approximately 1,240 records, with access, scope and notification unresolved. | Preserve logs, investigate access and scope, require updates and assess notification/remediation obligations on evidence. | **Keep diligence and protective obligations open.** Neither a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty nor any numeric demand is established. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 aggregate characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Read DD-008 and DD-011 together; assess timing, scope, accrual, termination rights and unavoidable commitments before classification. | **Investigate; do not automatically classify as Debt or deduct price.** Neither ordinary-course treatment nor a debt adjustment is established by the supplied facts. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations presumptively cover all Claims, including through exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses. | Expressly separate Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories, with clear precedence and no hidden general-regime override. | **Rewrite scope and cross-references throughout.** Separate protections are ineffective if blanket provisions silently override them. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register evidences ownership of 100% of shares. | Independent ownership, title, encumbrance and authority evidence, reconciled against the supplied register. | **Require independent verification before Completion.** DD-012 is an internal source, not independent proof of transferable, unencumbered title. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties considered settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax/IP terms expressly open and negotiate their scope, limitations and remedies separately; assume neither unlimited liability nor agreement. | **Reject “settled” status and reserve both categories.** Seller assertions do not establish buyer approval or resolve outstanding terms. |
=== END ADVICE ===
